text:
Twenty games into the first season of a rebuild, the Canucks have seven points and haven't won in six (0-6-0), outscored 25-13. Daniel and Henrik Sedin spent this week preaching patience, as Daniel Wagner of Pass it to Bulis reported, and the newest face in the room is defenceman Cameron Crotty, claimed off waivers from Minnesota. There's one odd thread of hope in the numbers: by the chances they've created and allowed, Vancouver would have about 14 points, not seven. The bad news is that the losing streak itself is earned. The Canucks have had 43% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) during it, and our playoff odds have them near zero.

The Rangers arrive in the opposite mood: 4-1-0 in their last five, and they won the chance battle in all five, with 61% of the expected goals. The one loss, 3-1 in Edmonton, came on a night they had 65% of the chances. At five on five New York has taken 53% of the expected goals this season to Vancouver's 41%, and the Canucks give up 3.74 expected goals per 60, while taking about four penalties a game. The Rangers won the October meeting 6-2, a game they deserved 82% of the time.

In net, Dylan Garand is projected for New York at +1.7 goals saved above expected, and he's had a crowded week around him: James Reimer's contract was terminated after he cleared waivers, and Joonas Korpisalo is back from a long stint on injured reserve. Leevi Meriläinen projects for Vancouver at -2.1 this season after -17.9 last year.

Brock Boeser is one point from 500 and on a five-game point streak, playing 21:00 a night with Filip Chytil out. Filip Hronek needs one goal for 50. J.T. Miller returns to Vancouver, where he played before his 2025 trade to New York, without a goal in six games on 3.2 expected goals, while Marcus Pettersson makes his first trip back after 113 games as a Canuck. Our Sleepers are both Rangers: Oliver Bjorkstrand (18% to score) and Tye Kartye (51% for a point).
headline: Canucks host Rangers, still searching for a win
